questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, only the right-hand side $b_i$ changes, to $b_i+\delta$. Which entries of the final simplex tableau of $\mathcal{B}^*$ change?
options: The slack columns, since $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ has to be recomputed for the new $\boldsymbol{b}$.
Only the right-hand-side column, that is, $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ and the value $Z^*$.
The objective row, since every reduced cost shifts by $y_i^*\delta$, with $y_i^*$ the shadow price.
The column under $x_i$ and the right-hand side, since $b_i$ belongs to the variable $x_i$.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$ and slack variables $s_1,\dots,s_m$, $b_i$ changes to $b_i+\delta$. Besides $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$, which vector decides which $\delta$ keep $\mathcal{B}^*$ feasible?
options: The $i$-th row of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, read along the row of the $i$-th basic variable.
The column under the decision variable $x_i$ in the final tableau of $\mathcal{B}^*$.
The $i$-th column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{e}_i$ of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, found under the slack $s_i$.
The column of $\boldsymbol{B}$ itself that belongs to the $i$-th basic variable.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$ and slack variables $s_1,\dots,s_m$, $b_i$ changes to $b_i+\delta$ with $\delta$ inside the range where $\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal. At what rate does $Z^*$ change per unit of $\delta$?
options: At rate $y_i^*$, the $i$-th entry of $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, read under $s_i$.
At rate $(\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b})_i$, the current value of the $i$-th basic variable.
At rate $c_i$, the objective coefficient of the decision variable $x_i$ in $Z$.
At the objective-row entry under $x_i$, the reduced cost of the variable $x_i$.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, $b_i$ changes to $b_i+\delta$ with $\delta\neq0$ inside the range where $\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal. Which statement about the optimal basis and its basic values is correct?
options: Both the basis and all basic values stay the same; only the optimal value $Z^*$ changes.
The basic values stay the same, but a different basis becomes optimal for the new data.
All variables, basic and nonbasic, are scaled by the same factor $(b_i+\delta)/b_i$.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal, but its basic values $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}'$ move with $\delta$.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, ranging the right-hand side $b_i$ gives $\delta_{\min}\leq\delta\leq\delta_{\max}$ with $\delta_{\max}$ finite. What holds for the change $\delta=\delta_{\max}$?
options: $\mathcal{B}^*$ is already infeasible there, since the range excludes its endpoints.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ is still optimal and a basic variable equals $0$, so the solution is degenerate.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ is still optimal and every basic variable is still strictly positive.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ is still optimal, but the shadow price $y_i^*$ has dropped to $0$ there.

questions.question: For $\max Z=2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq7$, $x_1+2x_2\leq10$, $x_1\leq5$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slack variables $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(4,3,1)^{\top}$ and the column of $s_2$ is $(-1,1,1)^{\top}$. For which $\delta$ does this basis stay optimal when $b_2=10$ becomes $10+\delta$?
options: $-3\leq\delta\leq4$
$-4\leq\delta\leq1$
$-1\leq\delta\leq4$
$\delta\geq-1$

questions.question: For $\max Z=6x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $2x_1+x_2\leq8$, $x_1+3x_2\leq12$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal value is $Z^*=28$, the optimal dual solution is $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(4,1,0)$, and the optimal basis stays optimal for $\tfrac{13}{2}\leq b_2\leq10$. What is the optimal value when $b_2=8$ is lowered to $7$?

The final simplex tableau of $\max Z=3x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $x_1-x_2\leq2$, $-x_1+x_2\leq3$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ (slack variables $s_1,s_2,s_3$) is optimal with basic values $x_1=4$, $x_2=2$, $s_3=5$, and its $s_1$-column reads $(\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2},0)^{\top}$ in that row order. Which values of the first right-hand side $b_1$ keep this basis optimal?
options: $2\leq b_1\leq10$
$b_1\geq2$

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+4x_2$ subject to $2x_1+x_2\leq16$, $x_1+2x_2\leq14$, $x_1+x_2\leq9$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slack variables $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_1)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1&2\\0&1&-1\\1&1&-3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(4,5,3)^{\top}$. If $b_2=14$ is lowered to $10$, does this basis stay optimal?
options: Yes: the basic values become $(4,1,7)$, all of them nonnegative.
No: the basic value of $s_1$ becomes $-1$, so the basis is infeasible.
No: $x_2$ drops to $-5$, which violates $x_2\geq0$ for this basis.
Yes: optimality depends only on reduced costs, which do not involve $\boldsymbol{b}$.

questions.question: For $\max Z=4x_1+5x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $x_1+3x_2\leq12$, $x_1\leq5$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slack variables $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis is $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ with values $x_1=3$, $x_2=3$, $s_3=2$. For which values of $b_3$ does this basis stay optimal, and what is the shadow price $y_3^*$?

For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal final tableau has objective row $-\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}+\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}$, with $s_i$ the slack of row $i$. Inside the range of $b_i$, what is the sign of the slope of $Z^*$ in $b_i$?
options: Nonpositive, since in an optimal tableau every objective-row entry is at most $0$.
Strictly positive, since at an optimum every resource has a positive unit worth.
Positive for $\delta>0$ and negative for $\delta<0$, following the direction of change.
Nonnegative, since it is the objective-row entry under $s_i$, which is at least $0$.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, ranging $b_i$ gives the interval $[\delta_{\min},\delta_{\max}]$ of all changes $\delta$ for which $\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible. Why is at least one end of it finite?
options: Because every entry of $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ is strictly positive at an optimal basis.
Because the shadow price $y_i^*$ is strictly positive at every optimal basis.
Because $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ is invertible, so $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{e}_i$ has a nonzero entry.
Because the feasible region is bounded, so $b_i$ cannot grow without limit.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, ranging $b_i$ gives $\delta_{\min}\leq\delta\leq\delta_{\max}$ with $\delta_{\max}$ finite. Which statement about $\mathcal{B}^*$ is correct for a change $\delta>\delta_{\max}$?
options: $\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible, but one of its reduced costs becomes negative.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays optimal, and the optimal value is still $Z^*+y_i^*\delta$.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ is infeasible, while its reduced costs all stay nonnegative.
$\mathcal{B}^*$ stays feasible, since raising $b_i$ only enlarges the feasible region.

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+4x_2$ subject to $x_1+2x_2\leq10$, $3x_1+2x_2\leq18$, $x_2\leq4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slack variables $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ has values $(4,3,1)$, $s_2$-column $(\tfrac{1}{2},-\tfrac{1}{4},\tfrac{1}{4})^{\top}$, $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{1}{2},0)$, $Z^*=24$. If $b_2=18$ rises to $22$, what are the new optimum and $Z^*$?

For $\max Z=3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq5$, $x_1+2x_2\leq8$, $x_1\leq4$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slack variables $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_2)$ has basic values $(4,1,2)$ and the column of $s_1$ is $(0,1,-2)^{\top}$. As $b_1=5$ is raised, up to which value does this basis stay optimal, and which basic variable is $0$ there?
options: Up to $b_1=7$, where $s_2=0$
Up to $b_1=6$, where $x_2=0$
Without upper limit, as no basic value decreases
Up to $b_1=6$, where $s_2=0$

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, an optimal basis gives value $Z^*$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^{*\top}=\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$. If $b_i$ becomes $b_i+\delta$ with $\delta$ outside the range and the new optimum is $Z'$, how does $Z'$ relate to $Z^*+y_i^*\delta$?
options: $Z'\leq Z^*+y_i^*\delta$ for all such $\delta$, by weak duality with $\boldsymbol{y}^*$.
$Z'=Z^*+y_i^*\delta$, because $\boldsymbol{y}^*$ does not depend on $\boldsymbol{b}$.
$Z'\geq Z^*+y_i^*\delta$, because a new basis can only do better than the old one.
$Z'\leq Z^*+y_i^*\delta$ above the range, but $Z'\geq Z^*+y_i^*\delta$ below it.

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$, basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, row $k$ has basic value $0$, all other basic values are positive, and $(\boldsymbol{B}^{-1})_{k,i}>0$. What does ranging $b_i$ with $\mathcal{B}^*$ give?
options: $\delta_{\min}=-\infty$, since a row with basic value $0$ gives no condition.
$\delta_{\max}=0$, since the zero row forbids any increase of $b_i$.
$\delta_{\min}=\delta_{\max}=0$, since a degenerate basis cannot be ranged.
$\delta_{\min}=0<\delta_{\max}$: the basis covers increases of $b_i$ but no decrease.

questions.question: For $\max Z=5x_1+3x_2$ subject to $2x_1+x_2\leq14$, $x_1+x_2\leq9$, $x_1\leq6$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal solution is $(5,4)$ with $Z^*=37$, the optimal dual solution is $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(2,1,0)$, and the optimal basis stays optimal for $9\leq b_1\leq15$. What is the optimal value if $b_1=14$ is raised to $17$?
options: $Z^*=43$, as $37+2\cdot3$ with the shadow price $y_1^*=2$
$Z^*=39$, attained at $(6,3)$ where $x_1+x_2\leq9$ and $x_1\leq6$ bind
$Z^*=37$, since the old solution $(5,4)$ stays optimal
No optimum: the old basis turns infeasible, so the program has no feasible point

questions.question: For $\max Z=5x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq6$, $3x_1+x_2\leq12$, $x_2\leq5$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2,s_3)$ ($s_i$ slack of row $i$) has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix}-1&1&0\\3&-1&0\\-3&1&2\end{pmatrix}$; one change at a time, it is optimal for $4\leq b_1\leq\tfrac{22}{3}$ and $8\leq b_2\leq18$. Is it optimal for $b_1=7$, $b_2=9$ together?
options: Yes: each change lies inside its own range, so together they keep the basis optimal.
No: the basic values become $(-2,3,-3)$, so $x_1<0$ and the basis is infeasible.
No: $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}'=(1,6,-1)^{\top}$, so $s_3<0$ and the basis is infeasible.
Yes: $x_1=1$ and $x_2=6$ are nonnegative, and $s_3$ keeps its value $2$ as $b_3$ is fixed.
